text:
lia (Support): FYI customer hit a consistent `401 invalid_api_key` after migrating secrets to their new secrets manager. They pasted the stored value we asked for and still get 401 from our hosted API. Repro steps from them attached.

sam (Eng Oncall): Can you paste the exact header they send (masked)? We should check for encoding issues.

lia (Support): Masked header they sent: `Authorization: ApiKey AXm_4a-9z..._Q` (they used `-` and `_` in the token, looks like urlsafe base64 chars).

maya (SRE): Ah that pattern screams base64url. Did they base64 the key for storage? Some secrets managers expect base64, but customers sometimes use a URL-safe variant.

toni (Support): Customer said they ran `echo -n "$KEY" | base64` when importing. They later said they copied the value from a web tool that produced `-` and `_` (no `+` or `/`).

sam (Eng Oncall): Ok this is the root cause: our API keys are standard base64 (plus `+` and `/`), not base64url. If their secret store converted the key to base64url (or they re-encoded with a urlsafe flag), the string will not match the canonical key and our auth will fail with 401.

lia (Support): Repro (internal): I tried a quick check. I took a valid key `AXm+4a/9z==` (masked) and converted it to base64url: `AXm_4a-9z`. Curl with the urlsafe string -> 401. Curl with original base64 -> 200.

lia (Support): repro commands I used:
```bash
# urlsafe (fails)
curl -s -H "Authorization: ApiKey AXm_4a-9z" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models | jq .error
# original (works)
curl -s -H "Authorization: ApiKey AXm+4a/9z==" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models | jq .models
```

maya (SRE): Thanks for the repro. Two remediation options: 1) ask customer to store the raw key (no re-encoding) in the secret store; 2) if they must base64-encode, ensure they use standard base64 (not base64url) and preserve padding `=`. We should give them a script to convert back if needed.

sam (Eng Oncall): Quick conversion they can run:
```bash
# convert base64url -> standard base64 (adds padding)
urlkey="AXm_4a-9z"
standard=$(printf "%s" "$urlkey" | tr '-_' '+/' ; pad=$(( (4 - ${#standard}%4) %4 )); printf '%*s' "$pad" "" | tr ' ' '=' )
# or simpler in python
python -c "import base64; print(base64.urlsafe_b64decode('AXm_4a-9z' + '==').decode(errors='ignore'))"
```
(we left the example minimal & masked)

toni (Support): I sent the conversion steps to the customer and recommended rotating the key after they fix storage. They applied the fix and reported `200` responses.

lia (Support): Resolution notes: cause = key re-encoded/stored as base64url (chars `-`/`_` and missing padding) -> auth mismatch -> `401 invalid_api_key`. Fix = restore raw key or convert base64url back to standard base64 (replace `-`->`+`, `_`->`/`, add `=` padding) OR just upload the original key. Customer rotated key & confirmed success. :white_check_mark:

maya (SRE): Can we add a short KB and a one-liner detection tool for this? I can add an infra-bot check to validate keys uploaded via our support tooling and warn if they look urlsafe.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4821 to add an automated validation on support-uploaded keys.

sam (Eng Oncall): Good call. Also pinged docs to add a note in the 'storing API keys' guide about not using urlsafe base64.

lia (Support): Closing here — customer confirmed they rotated and are green. Adding to support playbook entry.
